narrative.weekly_mirror: This week held both a connection to the practices you were raised with and a choice that was distinctly your own: you took the boys to the Ganesh temple, while Vihaan recited the first twenty verses “unprompted.” You also called Priya and said yes to the February order—“Twelve runners, twenty napkins”—moving through feeling “terrified and then calm.”
narrative.tension_explanation: The dinner earlier in the month still sits in contrast: “nobody asked me a real question about it,” even as the order became something you chose and named for yourself. The week seems to hold these experiences side by side—being part of family customs while wanting your own decision to be taken seriously.
narrative.reflective_question: What was it like to make room for your own choice while continuing to take part in the customs and family life that matter to you?
